title: minimal-service-account-patterns-and-policy-orchestrator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Provide a reusable Terraform module and associated CI workflows that produce minimal, auditable service-account and role bindings for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must make least-privilege the default: opinionated service-account naming, permission boundaries, ephemeral credentials patterns, policy templates for common workloads (model-serving, metrics ingestion, logging), and optional OPA/Sentinel policy checks. Deliverables: 1) terraform module (registry-style) that outputs role templates and binding resources, 2) a policy generator CLI helper for team-level overrides, 3) CI checks (terraform plan guardrails, terraform-compliance tests) and a documented upgrade/playbook for policy changes, 4) telemetry hooks (audit log links + drift detection webhooks), 5) example overlays for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes to internal registry with semantic versioning and docs
Default module configuration grants only required permission sets for three reference workloads
CI gates fail on policy regressions and produce clear remediation steps
Permission boundary support with explicit allow-lists for cross-account roles
Playbook for upgrading role templates with rollback steps and canary policy rollout pattern

notes: Design decisions: use permission boundaries + explicit role templates instead of broad managed policies to reduce lateral scope.
Trade-offs: more templates increases maintenance burden; mitigated by small generator CLI and template inheritance.
Rollout plan: canary by team -> org-stage -> org-wide with automated plan diff review and scheduled maintenance window.
Telemetry: wire terraform plan outputs to rollout dashboard; capture plan diffs to S3 and link in PR description for reviewers.
Future work: integrate with ephemeral session operator (short-lived SA tokens) and RBAC sync operator for on-prem air-gapped clusters.
